capabilities.nix-ownership: Use a compatible existing Nix daemon and its configured signed caches without changing the system configuration.
capabilities.clean-client-install: Install the exact tool pair from a clean client using published cached closures without compiling the tools locally.
capabilities.command-and-consumer-flow: Resolve both commands from a fresh shell and run the installed candidate through the generated project contract.
capabilities.paired-lifecycle: Rerun, select a version, update, roll back, interrupt, cancel, and uninstall the pair safely.
capabilities.failure-recovery: Stop at invalid prerequisites or failed operations with accurate partial state and recovery guidance.
capabilities.terminal-experience: Preserve the accepted Dashboard direction and equivalent still and plain output.
capabilities.timing-and-diagnostics: Measure stages and keep private, sanitized, bounded local records.
capabilities.windows-wsl-routing: Dispatch from native PowerShell into the selected eligible WSL2 distribution without installing Windows tools.

lanes.environment: Linux x86-64 with active systemd and the standard multiuser daemon.
Linux ARM64 with active systemd and the standard multiuser daemon.
Apple silicon macOS using the standard launchd service.
Native Windows PowerShell dispatching through actual wsl.exe into eligible x86-64 WSL2 with active systemd.
Native Windows PowerShell dispatching through actual wsl.exe into eligible ARM64 WSL2 with active systemd.

cases.requirement: Detect a compatible existing Nix installation and preserve its variant, mode, owner, projects, and configuration.
With administrator-configured features, cache URLs, and trusted public keys, verify signed substitution as an ordinary user. Preserve daemon settings and signature checks.
Rerun without changing the Nix version or daemon configuration.
Record initial store state and prove actual candidate closures come from configured caches on a clean client.
Install the exact native bootstrap and separate neo and neoctl commands as one lockstep pair without compiling either tool locally.
Resolve both owned commands in a fresh shell and stop before overwriting or hiding a conflicting command.
Run the generated neoctl executable with help, version, invalid arguments, and no arguments.
Use installed neo to generate, build, test, and run the pinned starter, then verify its health response and maintained smoke assertions.

Use two compatible complete candidate versions. Verify safe reruns, explicit supported-version selection, unchanged project pins, and preparation and activation of both tools together. Failed updates leave the prior pair usable.
Retain one previous working complete pair. Prove neo update --rollback restores it; failed updates leave the active prior pair usable. Rollback does not reverse Nix or system configuration.
Use the downloadable installer for lifecycle operations when installed neo cannot start.
Interrupt before and during activation; verify the old pair stays usable, cancellation reports changes, and rerun resumes only safe owned work.

Remove owned tools, generations, links, PATH additions and retained diagnostics. Preserve Nix, shared cache configuration, unrelated packages, project pins and contents, user shell edits and exported reports. Refuse or report cleanup with unproven ownership. Never delete store paths directly or run broad garbage collection.

Exercise transient download retry and exhaustion, integrity failure, missing prebuilt packages and insufficient permissions. For every negative case assert exit result, cause, actual partial state, report location and a usable recovery action.

Exercise missing, damaged, inaccessible or incompatible Nix, missing or untrusted caches, and unsupported architectures. Assert exit result, cause, actual partial state, report location and recovery without automatic repair.

Exercise quiet work, input waits, operation timeouts and partial-state inspection. Assert exit result, cause, actual partial state, report location and usable recovery. Inspect effects after timeout instead of blindly repeating system changes.
Compare the production Dashboard with the accepted archive and verify one review before user-owned changes, explicit script consent, and Details.
Verify still mode, equivalent plain output, cancellation, narrow terminals, live resizing, and accessibility behavior.
Verify prompts, progress, errors, recovery, help, completion, bootstrap, and Windows-routing text come from the English language file.

Measure feedback before network work and bootstrap, prerequisite, download, and completion stages. Separate machine time from human waits and record machine, network, and cache conditions. Verify elapsed time, last activity, input-needed state, finite retries, and derive response, timeout, and retry limits before release.

Create private records on every run. Seed controlled secrets, identifying paths and unsafe upstream output; verify sanitization in saved records, Details and exports. Assert required fields and failure report location. Test the seven-day boundary, repeated failures at the total 10 MiB cap, next-run pruning and no background cleanup.
Record sanitized failures before Rust starts without passwords, tokens, environment dumps, project contents, or identifying paths.
Inspect code and network activity for no installer telemetry or automatic report uploads, while allowing required release and cache downloads.
Install on NixOS with caches configured through nix.settings. Verify that both the declarative source and generated files are preserved.
Install on macOS with caches configured through nix-darwin. Verify that both the declarative source and generated files are preserved.

Exercise default and explicit distro selection, unsuitable or ambiguous defaults, consent, WSL2 presence, architecture, systemd, permissions, Linux identity, and actual wsl.exe dispatch. Run the successful case as a user without sudo access.
Show the selected distro and WSL-only command boundary before and after dispatch; verify no native tools, misleading wrappers, conversion, restart, install, or repair.
Record failures before Rust starts and during native-Windows routing with a report location and sanitized technical details.

conditional_case_policy: A conditional case is required when its condition applies. Unknown applicability or missing execution evidence keeps acceptance incomplete.
evidence_policy: This registry contains requirements only. It contains no pass results, support claims, or platform acceptance evidence.
